verdict.rationale: Open WebUI's own docs describe in-product agentic delegation. Native Function Calling (Agentic Mode) lets models explore the web autonomously, sub-agents hand off focused work in parallel, and Open Terminal lets the AI install dependencies, write and run apps, or hand tasks to Claude Code/Codex chosen from the model picker. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that agentic delegation works reliably, and a bundled assistant that does not depend on the user connecting their own model provider.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Sub-agents let a model hand a focused piece of work to a second agent that runs in parallel, then use the result to continue.
By enabling Native Function Calling (Agentic Mode), you allow quality models to independently explore the web, verify facts, and follow links autonomously.
Your AI can install dependencies, write the app, start its server, and inspect the output.
Pick Claude Code, Codex or another listed agent from the model picker like any other model.
